html:
SMTO-BOOT-0049 — Another program is already using SMTO's network port

GUID: 65e1e33c-23bc-4bce-9dcb-5841bdc262c7
Slug: startup-port-in-use
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: startup

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't open the network address your browser uses to reach it because another program is already using it. That program may be a copy of SMTO that's already running.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open SMTO in your browser at its usual address. If it opens and shows your conversations, keep using that copy. SMTO may already be running, and a second copy can't use the same address.
  2. If you started SMTO with ./startup.sh in another terminal window, press Ctrl+C there or stop the installed app, then start SMTO once. Two copies started at the same time compete for the same address and the same data.
  3. If no SMTO is running, ask the person who manages this computer to find which program uses the port before stopping anything. The other program may be doing important work, so it must be identified first.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens at its usual address and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message from the terminal, including the error code, and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start a second copy of SMTO on a different port using the same data folder.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Startup failed because binding a listener returned EADDRINUSE: another process already listens on the configured host and port.

What this means

  • Another listener already owns this address and port. A second controller must not take over the same state directory merely by using a different HTTP port.

Why this can happen

  • Another listener already owns this address and port. A second controller must not take over the same state directory merely by using a different HTTP port.

How to diagnose it

  • The operating system refused a listener bind because the address is in use.
  • The intended instance binds its address without an ownership conflict.

How to fix it

  • Identify the listener on the Server port (default 8011), manual port (8013) or Console port (8015) with ss -ltnp on Linux, lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN on macOS or Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen in Windows PowerShell, and match its PID before stopping anything. Use the existing SMTO instance if it owns this data; change ports (./startup.sh --port or --manual-port, AOR_CONSOLE_PORT) only for a separately configured instance with its own data directory.
  • Identify the listener with ss -ltnp on Linux, lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN on macOS, or Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen in Windows PowerShell. Match its PID to the intended service before stopping anything.
  • Identify the existing listener. Use the existing SMTO instance or stop the intended conflicting service; choose another port only for a separately configured instance.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded condition and run the diagnostic again. Rechecking does not replay tasks or completed operations.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended instance binds its address without an ownership conflict.

What not to do

  • Do not replay completed work or weaken authentication and certificate checks to clear this diagnostic.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic describes the observed failure; it does not establish the outcome of earlier operations.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
